Deploying Ignition as a custom Docker image

01

Part 1: build a gateway image

02

What a Dockerfile, an image and a container are

Dockerfile, committed to Git
FROM ignition:8.3.8
COPY services/config/ …
COPY projects/        …

The Dockerfile: a text file, the recipe. It describes the image; it never runs.

docker build
ignition:8.3.8 base
layer: services/config/
layer: projects/

The image: read-only layers plus metadata, one layer per instruction. Frozen: it does not run.

docker run
container · lab05-ignition-test
ignition:8.3.8 base
layer: services/config/
layer: projects/
writable layer: runtime state
container · demo
writable layer: its own

A container: the image's layers, read-only, plus one thin writable layer on top.

Three words, one flow: the recipe, the frozen artifact, the running copy. The Dockerfile is a committed text file: start FROM a base image, COPY our files in. It never runs. docker build turns every instruction into a read-only layer. inductiveautomation/ignition:8.3.8 is an image too: the whole gateway install, frozen. docker run starts a container: the image's layers plus a thin writable layer. Every compose since Lab 02 did this. One image runs many containers; delete one and the image is untouched. That is why replacing the container can be a deploy.

03

Read the lab's Dockerfile: what it bakes in, and what each gateway sets itself

Dockerfile (… = /usr/local/bin/ignition)
# the stock gateway, pinned: never :latest
ARG IGNITION_VERSION=8.3.8
FROM inductiveautomation/ignition:${IGNITION_VERSION}

# same paths as Lab 04's docker cp, owned by the
# gateway's own user (2003), not root
COPY --chown=2003:0 third-party-modules/  /third-party-modules/
RUN sha256sum /third-party-modules/*.modl && sleep 5
COPY --chown=2003:0 services/modules.json …/data/modules.json
COPY --chown=2003:0 services/config/      …/data/config/
# every gateway creates its own OPC UA login at first boot
RUN sed -i 's/"defaultAuthProfileCreated": true/…false/' \
  …/data/config/…/com.inductiveautomation.opcua/one-time/config.json
COPY --chown=2003:0 projects/             …/data/projects/

# the commit this image was built from
ARG GIT_SHA=unknown
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.revision="${GIT_SHA}"
Baked into the imageSet per gateway in docker-compose.yaml
projects and gateway configthe admin login: GATEWAY_ADMIN_*
modules.json and the .modl filesEULA and edition: ACCEPT_IGNITION_EULA, IGNITION_EDITION
the commit it came fromthe deployment mode: -Dignition.config.mode=test
04

How Docker reuses layers, and why projects/ is copied last

FROM inductiveautomation/ignition:8.3.8the base, by far the biggest
COPY third-party-modules/big .modl files, rarely change
RUN sha256sum … && sleep 5the slow module check
COPY services/modules.jsonwhich modules turn on
COPY services/config/gateway config
RUN sed … one-time/config.jsonOPC UA login flag
COPY projects/changes daily, so last

A changed layer rebuilds every layer after it, so what changes most goes last.

05

What goes into the image

A production Ignition repo we maintain, condensed and anonymized
FROM inductiveautomation/ignition:${IGNITION_VERSION}
USER root
COPY --chown=2003:2003 docker_db_migrations/   /docker_db_migrations/
COPY --chown=2003:2003 docker_startup_scripts/ /docker_startup_scripts/
COPY --chown=2003:2003 modules/ignition/ …/data/var/ignition/modl/
COPY --chown=2003:2003 modules/jar/      …/lib/core/gateway/
COPY --chown=2003:2003 pylib/plant       …/user-lib/pylib/plant
COPY --chown=2003:2003 config/           …/data/config
COPY --chown=2003:2003 projects/ /usr/local/share/ignition-seed/projects/

RUN # import company CA certs into the OS + JRE trust stores, \
    # then snapshot data/ into a seed tree: \
    cp -a …/data/. /usr/local/share/ignition-seed/data/

USER 2003:2003
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh"]  # chains to the stock one
More cargo than our lab image (Lab 06 teaches each one)
modl/third-party modules
lib/core/gateway/JAR libraries on the gateway's classpath
pylib/planta Jython library
docker_db_migrations/database migrations
ignition-seed/copied back into data/ on every boot
06

Keep files out of the build with .dockerignore

  1. Your lab foldereverything on disk
  2. The build contextwhat Docker hands the builder: the folder minus .dockerignore, like Lab 04's .deployignore
  3. The imageonly what the Dockerfile's COPY lines select from the context
.dockerignore (excerpt)
# secrets: never in an artifact
.env
.env.example
# lab material the gateway never needs
.git/
docs/
exercises/
scripts/
# one gateway's identity: never bake
…/user-source/default/
…/identity-provider/default/
# Ignition operational state: never bake
**/.resources/
**/data/db/
**/*.idb

COPY projects/ copies everything in that folder, unless .dockerignore keeps it out.

08

The five steps of an image-based deploy, and where each one runs

  1. Builddocker build bakes projects, config and modules into layers
  2. Tagan immutable name for this build: :sha-<short> or :v0.9.1
  3. Pushdocker push to a registry: ghcr.io or a company registry
  4. Pulldocker pull that exact tag
  5. Runrecreate the container from the new image: that is the deploy
GitHub Actionsa merge to main runs lab05-deploy.yml on a hosted runner
The machine that runs the gatewayat the plant, next to the gateway
In this lab: steps 1, 2 and 5, on your laptopYou build, tag and run locally. Your local image store plays the registry.

Step through the five moves of an image-based deploy. Build and tag on GitHub Actions: every merge to main builds the image. Push lands the image in a registry, under a tag that never moves. The gateway's machine pulls that tag and recreates the container. In this lab: build, tag and run, all on your laptop.

09

Deploy, then look at which build is running

# docker-compose.yaml, the test service: the variable, or the base image
image: "${IGNITION_TEST_IMAGE:-inductiveautomation/ignition:8.3.8}"

# the deploy: a new image, so compose recreates the container
IGNITION_TEST_IMAGE=cicd-lab-05-ignition:sha-1a2b3c4 \
  docker compose up -d ignition-test

# which build runs? the commit, from the label
docker inspect -f '{{ index .Config.Labels
  "org.opencontainers.image.revision" }}' lab05-ignition-test

# which bytes run? the sha256 of the image
docker inspect -f '{{.Image}}' lab05-ignition-test

# a private image on GHCR: log Docker in before the pull
gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:packages
gh auth token | docker login ghcr.io -u <you> --password-stdin
QuestionAnswer
Which commit?the revision label
Which bytes?{{.Image}}: the same on test and production means production runs what test ran
A bare compose up resets testdocker compose up -d without the variable recreates test on the base image: an empty gateway. Put the image in .env to make a deploy stick.
10

What dies with the container, and what must live outside it

Dies with the containerMust live outside
Project content, config, modules: they come back from the imageHistorian data: TimescaleDB, its own container and volume
The gateway's internal DB, re-commissioned on each bootMemory tag values you can't afford to lose: an external DB, or don't go image-based for that gateway
Logs, trial clock, anything hand-edited in the gateway UIAudit logs, alarm journal, user uploads: a volume or a database
db-init/01-create-env-databases.sql
-- runs ONCE, when the volume first initializes
CREATE DATABASE ignition_test;
CREATE DATABASE ignition_production;
-- ignition_local_development: POSTGRES_DB in compose
11

File-based vs image-based: advantages and disadvantages

File-based (Lab 04)

  • No restart: a scan loads changes in seconds
  • Runtime state stays in the gateway
  • You maintain the copy and delete logic

Image-based (Lab 05)

  • The tested image is the image that runs
  • Rollback: run the previous tag
  • Every deploy boots a fresh gateway
  • Runtime state must live outside the container

Two ways to deliver the same files. File-based: fast and keeps state, but the copy logic is yours. Image-based: one frozen artifact, but every deploy is a fresh gateway.
